Guide to Payroll Tax Withholding and Reporting (December 2011)
Government of Nunavut, Department of Finance

Employers withhold 2% of the gross remuneration of each employee. Not subject: members of religious orders with a vow of poverty, and less than 5,000 a year earned in Nunavut by an employee who normally works outside it; withhold once the 5,000 can reasonably be expected to be exceeded. Remittance by the 20th day of the month after the reporting period; annual return, even nil, by February 28.
Nunavut Payroll Tax Application for Registration (February 2022)
Government of Nunavut, Department of Finance

A withholding or pay-as-you-earn payroll tax of 2% of all gross remuneration paid to the employees who work more than half their time for an employer in Nunavut, collected by the employer from each employee. Registration within 21 days after the first remuneration paid.
Government of Nunavut, Department of Justice
Sections 1 (remuneration), 3 (tax of 2% of the employee) and 5 (withholding by the employer); Payroll Tax Regulations, R-049-93, s. 2

Every employee pays a tax of 2% of the remuneration paid in the year, which the employer withholds. An employee who normally works outside Nunavut owes the tax on the days worked in it, and none on a remuneration of 5,000 or less in the year from the employer (prescribed amount of the regulations). Named Payroll Tax Act, 1993 until 2024.

Table of the Year's Maximum Insurable Remuneration

Year's Maximum Insurable Remuneration of Nunavut: 113,900 in 2025, 117,300 in 2026 (110,600 shared with the Northwest Territories in 2024). Average provisional assessment rate of 2.40 per $100 of assessable payroll in 2026; the rate of each industry subclass is on WSCC Connect.

Annual Payroll Report, the actual payroll of the previous year and an estimate of the current year, due February 28. Directors of a corporation, business owners and the self-employed are not covered automatically; Personal Optional Coverage from 37% of the YMIR up to the YMIR.
WSCC Policy Manual, Policy 02.01 Employer Assessments

Assessment = (assessable payroll / 100) x the rate of the industry subclass, the payroll of each worker capped at the YMIR; minimum assessment of 200. Payment by March 31, or by instalments of March 31, May 31, July 31 and September 30 for an assessment of 1,000 or more.
